title: HarborLimiter: phased throughput guards with adaptive routing and anomaly sentinels
creator: Liam Chen
description: Build and ship 'HarborLimiter' — an SLO-first control plane that applies batching/caching optimizations incrementally using phased throughput limits, cohort-aware routing, and lightweight anomaly sentinels to automatically pause/rollback unsafe config changes.
progress_updates: 2025-11-06: Kickoff meeting with runtime, infra, and product teams. Agreed success metrics and minimum viable safety controls.
2025-12-01: Prototype limiter prototype implemented in runtime: token-bucket limiter + per-cohort counters. Small e2e smoke tests green.
2026-01-15: Telemetry contract agreed (p50/p90/p99, qdepth, error_rate, headroom estimate). Dashboard skeleton created in Grafana.
2026-02-02: Integration with routing layer (policy engine) for SLO-aware split routing. Canary experiments scheduled.
2026-02-20: Anomaly sentinel v1 added using EWMA + MAD detection for latency and error spikes. Began chaos testing in staging.
2026-03-04: Initial canary run against low-traffic cohort (5%) completed; observed ~7% cost reduction with no p99 regressions. Minor spike in queue_depth at peak window; mitigation work identified.
2026-03-10: Implemented auto-pause hook and manual rollback playbook. Preparing for broader canary (20%).
decision_log: Use phased throughput caps instead of instantaneous global config swaps to reduce risk of sudden latency regressions.
Adopt EWMA+MAD anomaly detector for sentinel due to low compute cost and fast detection on streaming telemetry.
Route by cohort fingerprint (customer_id hash % bucket) to isolate experiments and preserve deterministic rollback.
Keep first rollout cohorts limited to read-heavy, low-complexity models to minimize behavioral variance.
Expose an explicit manual kill-switch in Console alongside automatic pause thresholds for SRE confidence during rollout.
tradeoffs: Phased caps increase rollout time and slow ROI capture versus aggressive full-rollout approaches.
Lightweight detectors reduce false negatives but may produce more false positives compared to expensive ML detectors — chosen for operational simplicity.
Per-cohort routing adds routing table complexity and can slightly increase request path latency (microseconds) in exchange for safer isolation.
review_feedback: PM (Sofia Martinez): Prioritize clear Console UX for status and rollback actions — must be one-click for Product Ops.
Design (Ethan Park): Dashboard needs a compact cohort view showing headroom and trend sparkline; provided wireframes.
Security (Noah Patel): Confirm limiter config persisted to audit logs and KMS-encrypted where necessary. Security review flagged as not required for first phase but audit trail must be present.
Runtime lead (Maya Johnson): Suggest instrumenting KV-cache hit-rate per cohort to detect cache regressions early; added to telemetry contract.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (staging): unit + integration tests, chaos latency injection, verify sentinel triggers and auto-pause.
Phase 1 (canary 5%): low-traffic cohorts, monitor p99/p90/throughput for 72h, manual review and signoff.
Phase 2 (canary 20%): broaden to multiple regions and model variants, enable auto-pause thresholds and run 7-day monitoring.
Phase 3 (ramp): 50% then 100% with progressive cap relaxation as confidence grows; automatic rollback if sentinel triggers twice within window.
Post-rollout: capture regression tests and debrief; convert configs to baseline optimizer suggestions.
metrics_and_slos: Primary SLOs: p99 latency <= 450ms, p90 latency <= 150ms for text-generation endpoints for target cohorts.
Throughput target: maintain >= 95% of baseline throughput during cap application for high-volume cohorts.
Operational alerts: error_rate increase > 0.5% absolute or relative p99 degradation > 15% triggers auto-pause.
Queue depth monitoring: sustained qdepth > 200 requests for >60s triggers immediate limiter tightening and alert.
tests_and_simulations: Load test harness: synthetic client generator with realistic prompt-length distributions and burst patterns (github.com/redwood/harbor-load-test PR #188).
Chaos: staged latency injection on KV cache and kernel slowdown experiments to ensure sentinel sensitivity without excessive false positives.
A/B evals: quality regression tests on representative prompt set to ensure batching/caching changes do not degrade output semantics.
Replay: historical traffic replay using last 30 days traces into staging to validate headroom and limiter tuning.
notes: Goal: deliver 10-25% unit cost improvements for eligible workloads while guaranteeing no more than a 5% chance of violating production p99 SLOs during rollout.
We will iterate detector thresholds in staging with synthetic traffic before any customer-facing canary.
Plan to release a postmortem template for any rollback that includes timeline, cause, and next steps.
